The Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL), also known as ISIS, did not invade Iraq in the traditional sense. Instead, they emerged as a militant group in Iraq following the U.S.-led invasion in 2003, taking advantage of the ensuing power vacuum and sectarian tensions. Their actions were primarily driven by ideological motivations and the desire to establish a strict Islamic state according to their interpretation of Sharia law.
